- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.11) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% in next 7–14 days.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, cap the peak at 1–2% below the immediate prior high.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion after a strong upward move, model often fails to correct — adjust forecast downward by 2–5% in 3–5 day horizon.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.22) and model forecasts are rising, reduce forecast by 3–7% to avoid overconfidence in reversal.  
- If model consistently forecasts higher than true outcome in 30-day horizon, apply a 1–3% downward bias to next 30-day forecast, especially if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating positive/negative swings, model often misjudges momentum — use 3-day moving average of sentiment to smooth forecast adjustments.
